revisions.question: A volunteer event is about to begin, but responsibilities are still unclear. What contribution comes most naturally to you first?

options.label: Set the first priorities and help people take ownership of them
Create an engaging way for volunteers to begin contributing
Help volunteers feel connected to one another and confident about where they fit
Map the essential tasks, resources, and order of operations

revisions.discriminator_and_balance: Yellow now expresses belonging and supportive connection rather than role assignment; all four options remain useful ways to help the event begin.

revisions.question: A neighborhood project has enough funding for only one improvement. What guides your recommendation first?

options.label: Which choice will create the clearest visible result
Which choice could generate the most participation and fresh energy
Which choice will strengthen residents’ connection to the shared space over time
Which choice has the strongest cost, maintenance, and feasibility case

revisions.discriminator_and_balance: Yellow now favors lasting community connection and continuity; visible impact, participation, belonging, and feasibility are all defensible priorities.

revisions.question: A new colleague feels overwhelmed by several competing demands. What kind of help comes most naturally to you?

options.label: Identify the most important priority and help them take the next action
Help them see possibilities and regain some energy for the work
Help them identify which relationships and commitments need steady attention first
Organize the demands into clear steps, resources, and dependencies

revisions.discriminator_and_balance: Yellow now prioritizes relational continuity and commitments rather than uniquely compassionate listening; each option supplies practical, mature help.

revisions.question: An afternoon unexpectedly becomes free with no obligations. What are you most naturally drawn to do?

options.label: Use the time to make visible progress on something I want to accomplish
Choose something spontaneous, social, or new that feels energizing
Spend the time in a comfortable way with someone I care about
Dive into something I have wanted time to understand properly

revisions.discriminator_and_balance: Green now expresses attraction to careful understanding rather than organization or productivity; all four are equally reasonable uses of free time.

revisions.question: When friends disagree about a shared plan and either option could work, I would rather keep discussing until the group feels comfortable than choose an option and let the tension fade afterward.
revisions.discriminator_and_balance: The item contrasts harmony before closure with reasonable closure followed by natural recovery; neither side implies greater emotional maturity.
